subject: Acme bake-off: test plan & next steps
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 13:10:00 -0800
Subject: Acme bake-off: test plan & next steps

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for a great discovery call earlier. Per our conversation, I wanted to capture next steps and a proposed bake-off plan so we can align on success criteria and owners. Attached is a starter plan (redwood-acme-bakeoff-plan.xlsx) — feel free to update.

High-level goals:
- Validate latency and cost vs the hyperscaler endpoints you mentioned (AWS/GCP) for your 75–200 token prompt workloads.
- Confirm output parity (topical accuracy + hallucination rate) on your production prompts.
- Verify integration and rollout workflow for private deployments if you decide to go that route.

Proposed tests (owners & timeline):
- Perf baseline (p95, throughput): Aditya — 1 week (sandbox)
- Cost benchmarks (per-token across configs): Aditya + Finance — 1 week
- Quality/eval (prompt set supplied by Acme): Marissa — 1 week
- Integration smoke tests (prefix caching, streaming): Vanessa + Acme Eng — 1 week

Success criteria (examples):
- p95 latency <= 1200ms at expected concurrency; 99th <= 2000ms (on dedicated config)
- Cost per 1k tokens <= target agreed during kickoff (we'll confirm)
- Quality delta vs hyperscaler <= 5% for top-1 factual correctness on your eval set

Next steps:
1) Can you share the prompt set and a small sample dataset (anonymized) by EOD Friday?
2) We’ll provision a sandbox workspace and give you access (link & creds below).
3) Schedule a 30-min kickoff for next Monday to confirm metrics and owners.

Attachments: redwood-acme-bakeoff-plan.xlsx (starter plan)

Thanks — looking forward.

— Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz | Account Executive
Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0143

Vanessa — thanks for the plan and the quick recap. A few clarifying items from our side before we lock the kickoff: 

1) Hyperscaler comparison: Can you include a short spec of the hyperscaler endpoints you plan to compare against (AWS SageMaker realtime endpoint, GCP Vertex AI predictions, and any managed LLM API)? We need to see parity criteria.
2) Security/data retention: we'll need explicit notes on data handling in the sandbox (retention, logs, access controls) and whether audit logs are available.
3) Test data: we'll send an anonymized prompt set — can you confirm acceptable formats (CSV/JSON) and max size?
4) Timeline: we prefer a two-week window for the bake-off (one week perf + one week quality). Is that feasible?

Attaching the initial security questionnaire we use for vendors (acme-questions.pdf) — please have your security contact review.

I'll loop in Tom (Eng) for technical alignment.

Thanks,
Sarah
Director, Platform Engineering | Acme Corp
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme bake-off: test plan & next steps

Thanks Sarah — good questions. Quick answers and updates: 

1) Hyperscaler spec: we'll include an appendix in the plan comparing the interfaces & config used for the comparison (model size, endpoint type, batch settings). We'll test against: AWS SageMaker real-time (ml.g5.xlarge equivalent), GCP Vertex AI predictions (n1-standard analog), and the public LLM API that Acme currently uses.

2) Sandbox security: sandbox instances are provisioned in an isolated tenant with 30-day retention by default; audit logs are available and we can enable longer retention on request. We'll have our security engineer send a short note to address questionnaire items in acme-questions.pdf.

3) Test data formats: CSV (rows = prompt, label columns) or newline-delimited JSON are both fine. Max single upload 200MB; for larger sets we can accept a shared GCS/S3 link.

4) Timeline: two-week window works for us. Proposed schedule:
- Week 1 (Perf/Cost): 1 Mar — 7 Mar
- Week 2 (Quality/Evals): 8 Mar — 14 Mar

I'm attaching an updated test-specs doc and the bake-off matrix we plan to use (redwood-test-specs.pdf, acme-bakeoff-matrix.xlsx).

Sandbox access (provisioned): https://redwood.ai/sandbox/acme-bakeoff?token=REDACTED
Credentials will follow via secure channel.

I'll book a 30-min kickoff for Mon, 1 Mar 10:00 AM PT — invite to follow.

— Vanessa

Subject: Re: Acme bake-off: test plan & next steps (technical notes)

Hi all — quick technical notes for the bake-off so Acme Eng can prepare. Keeping to the test matrix Vanessa shared.

Recommended perf tests:
- Run steady-state load at your expected concurrency (we suggest 8–16 concurrent clients for your reported traffic). Capture p50/p90/p95/p99 latencies and tail behavior.
- Test with cold start vs warmed KV cache to surface benefits of prefix/KV caching.
- Compare model quantization variants (FP16 vs 8-bit quantized) for latency/cost tradeoffs.

Quality tests:
- Use the provided eval harness (we'll put scripts in the sandbox) to compute top-1 correctness and a simple hallucination scoring rubric.
- Include generation sampling settings in the matrix (temperature, top_p). We'll run the same settings across all platforms to keep parity.

Integration checks:
- Streaming behavior (client cancels mid-stream, reconnections)
- Response schemas (for structured output) — ensure determinism when applicable

Credentials & endpoints (sandbox):
- API host: sandbox.redwood.ai/acme-bakeoff
- API key: will be provided securely to Acme Engs

Target metrics (examples):
- p95 <= 1200ms for 75–200 token prompts at target concurrency
- Cost per 1k tokens <= $X (we'll fill actual number in kickoff)

I’ve dropped a small set of helper scripts into the sandbox (test-scripts.sh) that run perf sweeps and compute the basic metrics. Reach out if you want a walkthrough before the kickoff.

— Aditya
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

- We’ll deliver an anonymized prompt set (CSV, ~20k rows) by EOD Wed, 4 Mar.
- Tom will be the primary Eng contact for the perf tests; I’ll be the project owner for quality and legal items.
- Kickoff confirmed for Mon, 1 Mar — Tom and I will join; if you can share the invite again (our calendar blocked differently) please do.

Success criteria: we agree to use the matrix in redwood-test-specs.pdf as the source of truth. We’ll aim to complete the two-week window (1–14 Mar) and then reconvene for results and decision.

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Looking forward.

— Sarah
